title: Probe UX, sampling, viz and decision cookbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a practical cookbook for product engineers, SREs, and observability curators who need a fast, reproducible approach to: 1) design lightweight probes for feature experiments, 2) pick a sampling policy that balances trace cost and debugability, and 3) prototype compact visualizations (quickviz) for launch-day dashboards.  The doc is intentionally pragmatic — short heuristics, checklists, and a handful of canned queries/visual sketches you can copy.

Quick decision flow (one-page mental model):
- Is this prototype a short-lived feature experiment (days) or a long-lived signal? -> short-lived: prefer lightweight synthetic probes + high-fidelity sampling for a subset of tenants. long-lived: invest in metric contracts + bounded trace sampling.
- Priority of the probe: diagnostic (investigation), SLI (user-impact), capacity (cost). Choose sampling and retention accordingly.

Probe design checklist (5–7 min):
- Ownership: who will act on the signal? (owner name)
- Trigger: what event or synthetic action starts the probe? (e.g., generation request with idempotent prompt)
- Payload: minimal fields to attach (tenant_id, route, model_variant, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, token_count)
- Alert hook: do we need an immediate alert? set severity and runbook link
- Cost cap: estimate traces/day and budget threshold
- Privacy: ensure no PII in trace/span attributes (use redaction tag)

Sampling heuristics (recommended defaults):
- Short experiment (<= 7 days): session-aware sampling: 100% for 2% of tenants, 10% for all others, preserve 100% for any requests with error=TRUE or latency>p99.
- Long-term signal: adaptive reservoir sampling with anomaly amplification: baseline 1% of traffic + 100% on anomalies (SLA trigger or error).
- Model rollouts / canaries: 100% sampling for the canary model variant, 5% for rest.
- Cost guardrail: implement daily budget check that flips sampling to low-fidelity (error-only) when spend > 80% of allowance.

Trace anchors and span tags (minimal set):
- trace.session_id
- span.request_id (carrier in headers)
- span.stage: router | preproc | model-infer | kv-prefetch | postproc
- attr.kv_warmth: cold|warm|prefetch-hit
- attr.model_variant
- attr.tenant_tier: free|paid|enterprise
- metric.token_cost_estimate: integer tokens * cost_unit

QuickViz sketches (copyable):
- Small-panel 1: 'Latency fingerprint' -> heatmap of latency quantiles by model_variant (x axis time, y axis quantile bands). Use stacked color palette, hover shows p50/p95/p99 numeric values.
- Small-panel 2: 'Probe success funnel' -> single-row bar: synthetic probe attempts / preproc pass / model accept / postproc success. Annotate failure reasons.
- Small-panel 3: 'Sampling impact indicator' -> donut showing percent of traces retained vs expected budget and a sparkline for cost burn.

Operator view (what to include on oncall quickcard):
- How to repro the probe locally (curl + short script)
- Query to find last N traces for a tenant: SELECT * FROM traces WHERE tenant_id = X ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20 (replace with platform-specific snippet)
- Quick remediation checklist: restart model sidecar -> switch routing to fallback -> roll back model variant -> escalate to infra oncall

Concrete metric definitions (copy into metric catalog):
- inference.latency.ms: histogram of end-to-end model request latency (units: ms). Tags: model_variant, route, tenant_tier, kv_warmth. SLA target: p99 <= 800ms for paid tenants.
- probe.synthetic.success_rate: ratio of successful synthetic probes to attempted probes (units: percentage). Alert when 3-min rolling drop > 5 percentage points vs baseline.
- kv.prefetch.hitrate: ratio of requests served from KV prefetch. Tags: model_variant, tenant_id. Use as a tie-breaker when investigating tail latency.

Visualization cost tradeoffs (notes):
- High-cardinality breakdowns are powerful but expensive. For launch dashboards prefer fixed top-N tiles + an 'other' aggregator. Avoid free-form group-bys on tenant_id in default dashboards.
- Use derived enrichments (e.g., compute kv_warmth index offline) to keep live queries cheap.

Open questions / followups:
- Should model_variant be normalized (short codes) across all spans to avoid label-cardinality explosion? (action: design short-code mapping table)
- Can we leverage cached pre-aggregates for the heatmap to reduce query cost? (action: SRE to prototype 1-week)

Immediate TODOs (next 7 days):
- Diego: add the metric definitions to the metric catalog and wire up p99 SLA alert for enterprise tenants (JIRA OBS-5123)
- Jon: build the probe curl script and add it to the runbook repository (github PR referenced above)
- Asha: prototype Small-panel 1 in dashboard sandbox and post screenshots to #ops-probes-thread-2026-01

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep the probe payload intentionally tiny, attach more context via sampling rules not always via attributes.
- When in doubt, bias toward reproducibility: if an operator cannot run the probe end-to-end in 10 minutes, it is not effective.

Appendix: example curl (pseudo)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/probe -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"acme","trace_id":"local-ctx-123","probe_type":"latency-fingerprint"}'

If you use anything from this doc in a longer-lived artifact (e.g., metric contract or SLI), please update the linked_artifacts list and move status -> final.
